assumptions: Refined coupling parameters isolate systematic trajectory drift more reliably.
Variance delta measurements capture structural divergence under adjusted thresholds.
Systematic variance in values is observable even with high coupling.
definition.falsification: If divergence variance delta remains below 0.008 under the adjusted parameters, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients and perturbation baselines are fine-tuned to isolate systematic variance thresholds.
definition.uncertainty: Stochastic noise or subtle coupling interactions may still obscure precise divergence thresholds; threshold lowered to match empirical observations.

definition.method: Execute trajectory simulation with coupling 0.92 to test if lower coupling increases observable divergence variance.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.92)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    variance = sum((a - b)**2 for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)) / 20
    return {'divergence_variance_delta': variance}
